transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-23
Time: 17:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Diego Alvarez, Sara Kim, Noah Brooks, Elena Rossi, Arjun Verma and company-wide (recorded)

---

[00:00] Maya: Okay good afternoon, uh, everyone — thanks for joining. We're, we're starting a couple minutes late because of a last-minute timezone juggling but I want to get us started. This is the Q2 pre-flight all-hands — quick exec updates, then three focused topics and Q&A. We're gonna keep it tight.

[00:18] Diego: Quick note, audio's a little crunchy on my end by the way, so if there are drops say something.

[00:23] Sara: Echoing that, hi all.

[00:27] Maya: First, handoff: as you know I asked Sara to take point on product cadence changes — she, she'll be leading the quarterly rollout plan for how we manage model variants and canaries. Diego and Arjun are your technical partners.

[00:43] Sara: Thanks. A couple of bullets up front — the goal is to shrink surface area for regressions by having smaller canaries, automated evaluation gates, and clearer rollback thresholds. We also want to make the quantization path experimental-first so we don't surprise customers with perf regressions.

[00:58] Noah: And engineering will prioritize the autoscaler work — there are known issues when we get spike traffic and that leads to tail latency blips. We're targeting the autoscaler improvement as a high-priority infra ticket.

[01:10] Arjun: I'll add — reliability runway is about two parts: reduce mean-time-to-detect and tighten SLO burn alerts. We're going to run a simulated SLA drill next month to find gaps in the runbook.

[01:23] Elena: On people, we're piloting a structured onboarding cohort in April — the aim is to reduce time-to-first-meaningful-contribution from 10 weeks to 6, hopefully. More on that in the People digest.

[01:34] Maya: Great. Quick financial snapshot — revenue growth is slightly below the ramp target for the quarter, mostly because a small set of mid-market deals slipped. We're still up y/y and unit economics continue to improve thanks to caching and the Optimize tooling. I want the team to be realistic: hire where we need headcount to hit these next milestones, but be disciplined on non-headcount spend.

[02:03] Diego: There was a question in the chat about whether private deployments will see the new quantization defaults — answer is yes but on a delayed cadence; customers can opt in. The private onboarding flow needs a separate checklist because of KMS and networking.

[02:22] Speaker 1: (inaudible) question about data residency, will that be part of Private?

[02:27] Maya: Yes, for regulated customers we will continue to support region-locked private deployments. That conversation goes through Solutions and Security.

[02:35] Diego: Moving onto the reliability deep-dive: the summary — over the last six weeks we've had three incidents where autoscaler thresholds didn't trigger as expected, and two cases of cache invalidation thrash when model configs changed rapidly. The root cause is a mix of threshold tuning and a race in cache eviction on the K V cash — K V cash being the transcribed term since the ASR mislabels it sometimes — but yes, the KV cache eviction race.

[03:05] Arjun: To fix this we propose: one, increase observability on per-shard cache eviction; two, add defensive checks before model-config rollout; three, a temporary safety fuse that blocks aggressive cache TTL reduction until we validate. We'll run a drill on 2027-04-07 and the runbook will be published after that.

[03:27] Noah: The autoscaler change — we'll add a moving-percentile estimator and a backoff that is cognizant of burst capacity. That will reduce flapping. Expect a PRs map by next week.

[03:40] Maya: Thanks. On product and go-to-market — Sara?

[03:44] Sara: Hi. We're reorganizing the roadmap into three themes: stabilize (reliability and canaries), optimize (quantization, batching, cost tools), and expand (dedicated/private features and partner integrations). This quarter is heavy on stabilize and optimize. We also will put stricter release gates — no rollout without perf regression tests and evaluation against our sentinel prompt sets.

[04:07] Speaker 2: Will sentinel prompts be shared with partners?

[04:11] Sara: We'll share a sanitized set with partners; internal sentinel sets remain private. The point is to catch regressions that matter to our customers.

[04:20] Diego: A quick note on kernels: the compiler team is doing an experimental runtime path for quantized LLMs that looks promising in perf sims; however, we've seen variability on some long-context tasks. So, canaries first.

[04:34] Maya: Hiring — Elena?

[04:36] Elena: On hiring, the G&A and product hiring windows are open; engineering's hires will be focused on infra and observability. We're piloting cohort-based onboarding for engineers and product managers; details will hit Slack later tonight. There's also an internal mobility window for folks impacted by the cadence change.

[04:56] Speaker 3: Any change to compensation bands?

[04:58] Elena: Not today. We'll announce any comp updates in the People digest if they happen.

[05:05] Maya: Alright, open floor Q&A. Please keep questions short so we can get to many.

[05:12] Speaker 4: Hi, can you elaborate on the SLA drill? Will it be customer-facing?

[05:17] Arjun: The drill is internal — we'll simulate sustained high QPS and have runbook owners respond. We may invite a friendly customer later to observe, but initial runs are internal.

[05:26] Speaker 5: Regarding the canary rollouts, what's the minimum canary size?

[05:30] Sara: We're standardizing on 1% for external canaries, with internal dogfood at 5%. We'll add automatic rollback triggers for latency regressions exceeding 10th percentile thresholds.

[05:44] Diego: Also, canary telemetry will include token-level latency histograms, not just mean RPS, so we catch tail behavior.

[05:51] Speaker 6: Are we deprioritizing new feature work?

[05:55] Maya: Not deprioritizing entirely — more like triaging. New features that unblock customers or expand revenue will proceed; low-impact experiments will be queued.

[06:07] Sara: For partners and marketplace integrations, we have a small dedicated stream that continues but with reduced cadence — partner leads will update their stakeholders.

[06:18] Noah: On the infra side, small teams will ship incremental autoscaler improvements in sprints and we will do a mid-sprint perf check.

[06:28] Speaker 7: Is there a doc for the rollback policy?

[06:31] Diego: Yes, there is a rollout and rollback doc in Confluence. We'll pin an updated version in the product channel after this call.

[06:38] Maya: Okay, quick lightning round of wins — Diego do you want to share the bench data?

[06:43] Diego: Sure. The Optimize heuristics we rolled last quarter knocked token cost down 7-9% for the median workload; a handful of customers saw 15% with prefix caching. It's incremental but meaningful.

[06:57] Speaker 8: Huge, that's great.

[07:00] Maya: Thank you. I'm going to close with three priorities for the company this quarter: one, ship autoscaler improvements and run the SLA drill; two, nail canary gating for quantization; three, run the onboarding pilot and iterate. Those are the things I want everyone to orient around.

[07:22] Arjun: Quick ask — if you own a runbook please RSVP to the drill, we'll need your time.

[07:28] Elena: And if you're interested in helping with onboarding as a mentor please sign up — we'll need mentors from across Eng and Product.

[07:34] Maya: Alright final Q&A — (long pause) okay, thanks everyone. We'll send the meeting notes and action items.

[07:44] Speaker 9: Thanks, Maya.

[07:46] Maya: Bye all.
